editorial:
You step into 1950s America with Ray Kroc, a tired salesman who spots a tiny burger stand run by Mac and Dick McDonald. Their fast, clean system blows him away, and he sees a chance to build something huge. The movie feels like a business dream turning into a tense power struggle, with Michael Keaton making Ray both charming and hard to trust. You watch him push for franchises, face pushback, and slowly change from hopeful partner to ruthless owner.

Keaton’s performance carries the film, and the pacing keeps you interested even when scenes are just meetings and deals. It is not packed with action, so if you want explosions, this may feel slow. But if you like true stories about ambition and greed, it is gripping. The supporting cast helps, and the period details make the world feel real. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ray uses his land deal to force Mac and Dick out of their own business. He buys them out, takes the McDonald’s name, and leaves them with almost nothing. The brothers are pushed aside while Ray builds a giant empire. The last moments show him rehearsing a proud speech, proving he now sees himself as the true founder, even though the brothers created the idea.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about ambition and business.
